name: Brazilian butt lift

lead: A Brazilian butt lift takes fat from elsewhere on the body by liposuction and injects it into the buttocks. The payoff people want is fuller, rounder glutes and a reshaped waist-to-hip silhouette, using their own tissue rather than an implant.

Fat is harvested, processed and injected into buttock tissue. Surgical reviews describe gluteal fat grafting as the fastest growing procedure in body contouring, with much of the recent literature on safety, anatomy and technique. Some transferred fat is reabsorbed, so volume can change over following months. On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed mainly as a female-appearance procedure, with some users asking about male equivalents.

paras: It is done by a plastic surgeon under anaesthesia, combining liposuction of donor areas with injection into the glutes. Swelling takes weeks to settle before the shape shows, and some people have repeat sessions. Some surgeons use ultrasound to visualise the injection plane. Travel for the procedure is covered in media reports.

Reported complications include fat resorption, asymmetry, infection, seroma and persistent numbness. A 2015 report from Mexican surgeons recorded 13 deaths from gluteal lipoinjection, and a 2019 meta-analysis reported complication rates of 7% for fat grafting versus 31% for implants. Safety technique has become a central focus of the field. It is a surgical procedure for licensed surgeons.

angle.text: Fat harvested by liposuction is injected into the glutes, adding volume and reshaping the waist-to-hip silhouette with your own tissue. The change shows once swelling settles; surgical reviews also document deaths, and safety technique is a major focus.

lead: Brazilian butt lift (BBL) is the common name for buttock augmentation using fat transfer, in which a patient's own fat is harvested by liposuction and injected into the gluteal region. [1][2] Wikipedia notes that the term probably comes from the Brazilian surgeon Ivo Pitanguy, who pioneered related surgery in the 1960s, while the Venezuelan surgeon Eduardo Krulig described buttock lipoinjection in 1987. [2]

Surgical reviews describe gluteal fat grafting as the fastest growing procedure in body contouring, and a large share of the recent literature focuses on safety, anatomy and technique. [1][3][4] A 2015 report documented deaths from gluteal lipoinjection among Mexican surgeons, and a 2019 meta-analysis put the complication rate for fat grafting at 7% against 31% for implants. [2]
In looksmaxxing forums the procedure is mostly discussed in terms of female appearance, with some users asking about male equivalents.

paras: Gluteal augmentation by autologous fat transfer is described in surgical texts as a way to transform the body silhouette, with proper patient selection, planning and technique said to be critical to safety and results.  Anatomy-focused reviews emphasise the clinically relevant structures to avoid complications. [3]

Surgeons have published on ultrasound-guided fat grafting, which lets the operator view the subcutaneous space during injection, and on harmony between the buttocks and whole-body contour. [4] Recovery involves compression garments and activity restriction, with final contour appearing months later. [2]

Reviews describe powerful and consistent results when the operation is carried out with careful planning.  Wikipedia notes that some of the transferred fat may be reabsorbed and repeat sessions may be needed. [2] An experience of over 3,000 patients and an assessment tool for optimising results have been described in the literature.

Evidence consists mainly of surgeon case series, reviews and technique papers. A report of experience with more than 3,000 patients was published in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery, and a separate paper introduced a BBL assessment tool.

A 2019 meta-analysis of 46 publications cited by Wikipedia found a complication rate of 7% for fat grafting versus 31% for implants. [2] No randomized trial of BBL compared with no surgery was identified.

Wikipedia reports that a 2015 study documented 64 liposuction deaths among Mexican surgeons, 13 of them from gluteal lipoinjection, plus nine deaths in Colombia. [2] Other complications include fat resorption, asymmetry, abscess, cellulitis and persistent numbness that can take up to two years to resolve. [2]
A Clinics in Plastic Surgery review on safety in gluteal augmentation describes efforts made to improve the safety of the procedure. [1]

One looksmax.org thread reproduces a list of male analogues of BBL and breast implants, including pectoral implants and male buttock augmentation by fat or implant; another poster objected that height is not an equivalent.
